## CONTEXT

This research is exploratory and observational. 

The four response variables are (i) spider abundance, (ii) spider family richness, (iii) carabid abundance, (iv) carabid species richness.

The predictor variables are (i) management type (conventional or organic), (ii) vegetation complexity (cover, height and species richness), (iii) proportion of natural area in surrounding landscape, (iv) habitat (vine row or inter row).



## LOCAL AND LANDSCAPE FACTORS

### Load Predictor Variable Datasets

Let's load the local and landscape data and combine into one dataframe using site_ID.

```{r}
# Load predictor datasets and vineyard coordinates
sites <- read_csv(here("00_data", "vineyard_sites.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
veg <- read_csv(here("00_data", "veg_data_VY.csv"))
landscape <- read_csv(here("00_data", "landscape_metrics.csv"))
coords <- read_csv(here("00_data", "site_coordinates.csv"))

# Ensure coordinates are numeric
coords <- coords %>%
  mutate(site_ID = as.character(site_ID)) %>%
  mutate(
    long = as.numeric(unlist(long)),
    lat  = as.numeric(unlist(lat))
  )

# combine into one dataframe using site_ID
vineyard_sites_df <- sites %>%
  left_join(veg,  by = "site_ID") %>%
  left_join(landscape,  by = "site_ID") %>%
  drop_na() 

```

Next we'll summarize the proportion of natural areas in the surrounding 1000m landscape and distance to nearest natural area by management type.

```{r}

    min_distance_natural    = min(distance_to_natural, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_distance_natural    = max(distance_to_natural, na.rm = TRUE),

summary_landscape
```

### Models for Vegetation Variables

Let's use LMM's to explore how vegetation properties vary by management type, habitat and year. 

```{r}
# Make sure factors are set correctly
veg_VY_data <- vineyard_sites_df %>%
  mutate(
    management_type = factor(management_type),
    habitat         = factor(habitat),  # CR / DR
    year            = factor(year)
  )

# 1) Vegetation cover (%): LMM (Gaussian)
lm_cover <- lmer(
  avg_veg_cover ~ management_type + habitat + year + (1 | site_ID),
  data = veg_VY_data
)

# 2) Vegetation height (cm): LMM (Gaussian)
lm_height <- lmer(
  avg_veg_height ~ management_type + habitat + year + (1 | site_ID),
  data = veg_VY_data
)

# 3) Vegetation richness: LMM (Gaussian)
lm_rich <- lmer(
  veg_richness ~ management_type + habitat + year + (1 | site_ID),
  data = veg_VY_data
)

# Summaries
summary(lm_cover)
summary(lm_height)
summary(lm_rich)

# R2 (marginal = fixed effects only; conditional = fixed + random)
performance::r2(lm_cover)
performance::r2(lm_height)
performance::r2(lm_rich)

```

Let's make sure the residuals look okay
```{r}
# Calculate residuals
residuals_cover <- residuals(lm_cover)

#Calculate predicted
predicted_cover <- predict(lm_cover)

# Plot the ordinary residuals against the fitted values
plot(predicted_cover, residuals_cover,
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted Values, Cover",
     xlab = "Fitted Values",
     ylab = "Residuals",
     pch = 16, col = "blue")

# Calculate residuals
residuals_height <- residuals(lm_height)

#Calculate predicted
predicted_height <- predict(lm_height)

# Plot the ordinary residuals against the fitted values
plot(predicted_height, residuals_height,
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted Values, Height",
     xlab = "Fitted Values",
     ylab = "Residuals",
     pch = 16, col = "blue")

# Calculate residuals
residuals_rich <- residuals(lm_rich)

#Calculate predicted
predicted_rich <- predict(lm_rich)

# Plot the ordinary residuals against the fitted values
plot(predicted_rich, residuals_rich,
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted Values, Richness",
     xlab = "Fitted Values",
     ylab = "Residuals",
     pch = 16, col = "blue")




```

Residuals versus fitted values do not indicate strong heteroskedasticity, with residual variance remaining relatively constant across the range of fitted values.

Finally let's make a summary table of the LMM's for the vegetation variables by management.

```{r}
# Tidy fixed effects tables for vegetation variable linear models
tidy_veg_models <- bind_rows(
  tidy(lm_cover,  effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>% mutate(Response = "Vegetation cover (%)"),
  tidy(lm_height, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>% mutate(Response = "Vegetation height (cm)"),
  tidy(lm_rich,   effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>% mutate(Response = "Vegetation richness")
) %>%
  dplyr::select(Response, term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value)


tidy_veg_models_fmt <- tidy_veg_models %>%
  mutate(
    estimate  = round(estimate, 2),
    std.error = round(std.error, 2),
    statistic = round(statistic, 2),
    p.value   = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", round(p.value, 3)),
  )

# save as table
write.csv(
  tidy_veg_models_fmt,
  here::here("02_tables", "veg_model_table.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)



# format nicely for word doc using flextable package
veg_table <- flextable(tidy_veg_models_fmt) %>%
  set_header_labels(
    Response   = "Response",
    term       = "Predictor",
    estimate   = "Estimate",
    std.error  = "SE",
    statistic  = "t value",
    p.value    = "p value"
  ) %>%
  autofit()

veg_table


```


### Check for collinearity

Let's check to see if the vegetation variables are collinear. 

```{r}
# Check collinearity among predictor vegetation variables
cor_matrix <- cor(veg[, c("avg_veg_height", "avg_veg_cover", "veg_richness")], 
                  use = "complete.obs")
cor_matrix

# Plot the correlation matrix
corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "circle", type = "upper", order = "hclust",
         addCoef.col = "black", # Color of the correlation coefficients
         tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45) # Color and rotation of the labels

```


The vegetation variables are moderately collinear (0.3-0.52), but below the 0.7 rule of thumb threshold. They can likely be modelled at individual predictors without causing problems.  


### Scaling predictor variables
Prior to modelling, let's scale the continuous predictor variables to enable comparisons. 

```{r}

    avg_veg_height, avg_veg_cover, veg_richness, total_natural_100, total_natural_250, total_natural_500, total_natural_750, total_natural_1000, distance_to_natural,
    z_veg_height, z_veg_cover, z_veg_richness, z_total_natural_100, z_total_natural_250, z_total_natural_500, z_total_natural_750, z_total_natural_1000, z_distance_natural
  )
```



## SPIDERS

### Data import and summarizing

Let's import the raw spider data and summarize by site/ habitat/ year. Let's also calculate the total number of spiders collected in vineyards, and the number of different families. Note that spiders that could not be identified to family level, either due to damage or being juveniles, are included in total spider count but not in family richness count.

```{r load-data}
# Load spider data
spider_VY_df <- read.csv(here::here("00_data","spider_VY_df.csv"))

# Summarize spider abundance by site_ID, habitat and year
spider_abundance_VY <- spider_VY_df %>%
  group_by(site_ID, habitat, year) %>%
  summarize(
    spider_abundance = sum(total_count, na.rm = TRUE),      # Sum, ignoring NAs
    trap_count = sum(!is.na(total_count)),         # Count of non-NA values
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Total number of spiders found in vineyards across all sites and years
total_spiders_VY <- sum(spider_VY_df$total_count, na.rm = TRUE)

# VY FAMILY RICHNESS
# Define the full set of site and habitat combinations
site_habitat_all <- spider_VY_df %>%
  distinct(site_ID, habitat, year)

# Identify family columns 
family_start <- which(names(spider_VY_df) == "family_richness") + 1
family_columns <- names(spider_VY_df)[family_start:ncol(spider_VY_df)]

# Then re-define unid and identified categories
unid_cols <- union("UNID.", "LYCOSIDAE..juvenile.")  # add the juveniles
family_columns <- setdiff(family_columns, unid_cols)

# Long format
spider_long_VY <- spider_VY_df %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(family_columns), names_to = "spider_family", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(count = as.numeric(count))

# Get a list of all families observed at least once
observed_families_VY <- spider_long_VY %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>% 
  distinct(spider_family) %>%
  arrange(spider_family)

# Total number of unique species across all vineyard sites and years
total_family_richness_VY <- spider_long_VY %>%
  filter(!is.na(count), count > 0) %>%
  distinct(spider_family) %>%
  nrow()

# Family richness per site × habitat × year (count only families with >0)
spider_richness_VY <- spider_long_VY %>%
  filter(!is.na(count), count > 0) %>%
  distinct(site_ID, habitat, year, spider_family) %>%
  count(site_ID, habitat, year, name = "family_richness")

# MERGE ABUNDANCE AND RICHNESS
# Merge the abundance and richness by site ID, habitat and year
# replace the one datapoint with family_richness of 0
spider_data_VY <- spider_abundance_VY %>%
  left_join(spider_richness_VY, by = c("site_ID", "habitat", "year")) %>%
  mutate(family_richness = replace_na(family_richness, 0))

cat("Total spiders in vineyards across all sites and years:", total_spiders_VY, "\n")

cat("Total spider family richness across all vineyard sites and years:", total_family_richness_VY, "\n")

print (observed_families_VY)

cat("Number of site × habitat × year combinations:", nrow(spider_data_VY), "\n")

```

Now lets make some figures to explore the family abundance and site occupancy, as well as make a family accumulation curve to evaluate sampling effort.

```{r}
# FAMILY ABUNDANCE AND SITE OCCUPANCY FIGURES
# Summarize total abundance per family
spider_family_VY_totals <- spider_long_VY %>%
  group_by(spider_family) %>%
  summarise(total_count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(total_count > 0) %>%            # <-- only keep families with > 0 individuals
  arrange(desc(total_count)) %>%
  mutate(spider_family = factor(spider_family, levels = rev(spider_family)))

# Reorder factor levels for plotting
spider_family_VY_totals <- spider_family_VY_totals %>%
  mutate(spider_family = factor(spider_family, levels = rev(spider_family)))

# Abundance plot
spider_abund_vy <- spider_family_VY_totals %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert family names to title case
    spider_family = str_to_title(str_to_lower(spider_family)),
    # Reorder by abundance (most abundant at the top)
    spider_family = fct_reorder(spider_family, total_count, .desc = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = total_count, y = spider_family)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey70", color = "black") +
  labs(
    x = "Number of individuals",
    y = "Spider family"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10)
  )

#  Calculate site occupancy = number of unique sites where each family was detected in VY
spider_occupancy_VY <- spider_long_VY %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>%  # exclude zeros if present
  distinct(site_ID, spider_family) %>%
  count(spider_family, name = "site_occupancy") %>%
  arrange(desc(site_occupancy))

# Reorder factor levels for plotting
spider_occupancy_VY <- spider_occupancy_VY %>%
  mutate(spider_family = factor(spider_family, levels = rev(spider_family)))

# Occupancy plot
spider_occupancy_vy <- spider_occupancy_VY %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert to title case first
    spider_family = str_to_title(str_to_lower(spider_family))
  ) %>%
  # Then reorder by site occupancy (descending)
  mutate(
    spider_family = fct_reorder(spider_family, site_occupancy, .desc = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = site_occupancy, y = spider_family)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey70", color = "black") +
  labs(
    x = "Sites detected",
    y = "Spider family"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10)
  )

spider_abund_vy
spider_occupancy_vy


# FAMILY ACCUMULATION CURVE
# Aggregate trap-level data to site-level totals
site_family_matrix <- spider_VY_df %>%
  group_by(site_ID) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(family_columns), ~ sum(as.numeric(.), na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Drop the site_ID column for the matrix
rownames(site_family_matrix) <- site_family_matrix$site_ID
site_family_matrix <- site_family_matrix[ , -1]

# Remove all-zero families
keep <- colSums(site_family_matrix, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
site_family_matrix <- site_family_matrix[, keep, drop = FALSE]

# Build accumulation curve
acc_site <- specaccum(site_family_matrix, method = "random", permutations = 1000)

# Prepare tidy dataframe for plotting
acc_site_df <- tibble(
  sites = acc_site$sites,
  richness = acc_site$richness,
  se = acc_site$sd
)

# Plot
spider_family_accumulation <- ggplot(acc_site_df, aes(x = sites, y = richness)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = richness - 1.96 * se,
                    ymax = richness + 1.96 * se),
                width = 0.3) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of sites",
    y = "Number of spider families observed",
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

spider_family_accumulation
```

Zodariidae was by far the most abundant family with over 2000 individuals, while Lycosidae was the second most abundant and occurred at the most sites.

The accumulation curve shows that spider family richness increases rapidly at first and then begins to level off, indicating that sampling effort was sufficient for capturing most families present in vineyards.

### Descriptive stats

First let's join the predictor variables to the spider response variables. 
Remove sites missing data (site 5 from 2024 was removed from analysis since the vines were pulled out, and site 36 was removed as it had just been replanted in 2025)

```{r}
# Full combined dataset (with predictor variables)
spider_data <- spider_data_VY %>%
  inner_join(predictor_variables, by = c("site_ID", "habitat", "year"))


# Remove incomplete rows (2 sites missing predictor variable data)
# convert others to factors
spider_df_clean <- spider_data %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(
    site_ID         = as.factor(site_ID),
    management_type = as.factor(management_type),
    habitat         = factor(habitat, levels = c("CR", "DR")),
    trap_count      = as.numeric(trap_count)
  )
```

Next let's take a closer look at the response variables (spider abundance and family richness)

```{r}
# select spider abundance and family richness columns
spider_response_variables <- spider_df_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(
    spider_abundance,
    family_richness)

# Compute summary statistics
spider_summary <- as.data.frame(
  apply(spider_response_variables, 2, function(x){
    c(
      mean   = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd     = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      min    = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      max    = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
      IQR    = IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  })
)

# Make rows readable
spider_summary


```


Spider abundance averaged 49 individuals per habitat and sampling period, with counts ranging widely from 0 to 261 individuals. Spider family-level richness had a narrower range (0–10 families) and averaged five families per habitat and sampling period. 

I also want to make summary tables for spiders by 1) management type, 2) habitat and 3) year

```{r}
# spider abundance and richness summary stats
response_summary_by <- function(data, group_var, group_label) {
  data %>%
    group_by({{ group_var }}) %>%
    summarise(
      spider_abundance_mean   = mean(spider_abundance,   na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_abundance_sd     = sd(spider_abundance,     na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_abundance_min    = min(spider_abundance,    na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_abundance_max    = max(spider_abundance,    na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_abundance_median = median(spider_abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_abundance_IQR    = IQR(spider_abundance,    na.rm = TRUE),

      spider_rich_mean        = mean(family_richness,    na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_rich_sd          = sd(family_richness,      na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_rich_min         = min(family_richness,     na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_rich_max         = max(family_richness,     na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_rich_median      = median(family_richness,  na.rm = TRUE),
      spider_rich_IQR         = IQR(family_richness,     na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Level    = as.character({{ group_var }}),  # <-- force common type
      Grouping = group_label
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Grouping, Level, everything(), -{{ group_var }})
}


# 1) By management type
summary_by_mgmt <- response_summary_by(
  spider_df_clean,
  management_type,
  "Management type"
)

# 2) By habitat
summary_by_habitat <- response_summary_by(
  spider_df_clean,
  habitat,
  "Habitat"
)

# 3) By year
summary_by_year <- response_summary_by(
  spider_df_clean,
  year,
  "Year"
)

# Combine into one long table
response_summary_all <- bind_rows(
  summary_by_mgmt,
  summary_by_habitat,
  summary_by_year
)

response_summary_all

# save as table
write.csv(
  response_summary_all,
  here::here("02_tables", "spider_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

Spider abundance and richness higher in organic vineyards, but also lots of variability. 
Very similar between vine rows (CR) and inter rows (DR)
Higher in 2025 compared to 2024.

## CARABIDS

### Data import and summarizing

Let's import the raw carabid data and summarize by site/ sampling location/ year. Let's also calculate the total number of carabids collected in vineyards, and the number of different species.

```{r}
# Load raw carabid data
carabid_VY_df <- read.csv(here::here("00_data", "carabid_VY_df.csv"))

# Summarize carabid abundance by site_ID, habitat and year
carabid_abundance_VY <- carabid_VY_df %>%
  group_by(site_ID, habitat, year) %>%
  summarize(
    carabid_abundance = sum(total_abundance, na.rm = TRUE),      # Sum, ignoring NAs
    trap_count = sum(!is.na(total_abundance)),         # Count of non-NA values
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Total number of carabids found in vineyards across all sites and years
total_carabids_VY <- sum(carabid_VY_df$total_abundance, na.rm = TRUE)

# Richness

# Identify species columns 
species_start <- which(names(carabid_VY_df) == "species_richness") + 1
species_columns <- names(carabid_VY_df)[species_start:ncol(carabid_VY_df)]

# Split identified vs unidentified (for richness)
unid_cols <- intersect(species_columns, c("UNID","UNID."))
species_columns <- setdiff(species_columns, unid_cols)

# Long format
carabid_long_VY <- carabid_VY_df %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(species_columns), names_to = "carabid_species", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(count = as.numeric(count))

# Get a list of all species observed at least once
observed_species_VY <- carabid_long_VY %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>% 
  distinct(carabid_species) %>%
  arrange(carabid_species)

# species richness per site × habitat × year
carabid_richness_VY <- carabid_long_VY %>%
  filter(!is.na(count), count > 0) %>%
  distinct(site_ID, habitat, year, carabid_species) %>%
  count(site_ID, habitat, year, name = "species_richness")

# Merge abundance and richness summaries by site, year and habitat
carabid_data_VY <- carabid_abundance_VY %>%
  left_join(
    carabid_richness_VY,
    by = c("site_ID", "habitat", "year")
  ) %>%
  mutate(species_richness = replace_na(species_richness, 0))


# Total number of unique species across all vineyard sites and years
total_species_richness_VY <- carabid_long_VY %>%
  filter(!is.na(count), count > 0) %>%
  distinct(carabid_species) %>%
  nrow()


# Extract genus from species name and count unique genera
total_genus_richness_VY <- carabid_long_VY %>%
  filter(!is.na(count), count > 0) %>%
  mutate(genus = stringr::str_extract(carabid_species, "^[A-Za-z]+")) %>%
  distinct(genus) %>%
  nrow()


cat("Total carabids in vineyards across all sites and years:", total_carabids_VY, "\n")
cat("Total carabid species richness across all vineyard sites and years:", total_species_richness_VY, "\n")

print(observed_species_VY)
cat("Total carabid genus richness across all vineyard sites and years:", total_genus_richness_VY, "\n")
cat("Number of site × habitat × year combinations:", nrow(carabid_data_VY), "\n")

```

Now let's make some plots to look at abundance and site occupancy by genus, as well as species accumulation to evaluate sampling effort.

```{r}
# VY Site occupancy and species abundance plots
# Summarize total abundance per species
carabid_species_VY_totals <- carabid_long_VY %>%
  group_by(carabid_species) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(total_abundance > 0) %>%           
  arrange(desc(total_abundance)) %>%
  mutate(carabid_species = factor(carabid_species, levels = rev(carabid_species)))


# Genus totals & occupancy (VY)
carabid_long_genus_VY <- carabid_long_VY %>%
  mutate(genus = str_extract(carabid_species, "^[A-Za-z]+")) %>%  # extract genus
  group_by(site_ID, habitat, genus) %>%
  summarise(count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

carabid_genus_totals_vy <- carabid_long_genus_VY %>%
  group_by(genus) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(total_abundance > 0) %>%  # remove genera with 0 abundance
  arrange(desc(total_abundance))

# create plot for abundance
genus_abund_vy <- carabid_genus_totals_vy %>%
  mutate(genus = forcats::fct_reorder(genus, total_abundance)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = total_abundance, y = genus)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey70", color = "black", width = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of individuals",
    y = "Carabid genus"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_blank(),                # remove title
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),      # larger axis titles
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(face = "italic", size = 10),  # italic + larger genus labels
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10)
  )


# plot for occupancy
carabid_genus_occupancy_vy <- carabid_long_genus_VY %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>%
  distinct(site_ID, genus) %>%
  count(genus, name = "site_occupancy") %>%
  arrange(desc(site_occupancy))

genus_site_occupancy_vy <- carabid_genus_occupancy_vy %>%
  mutate(genus = forcats::fct_reorder(genus, site_occupancy)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = site_occupancy, y = genus)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey70", color = "black", width = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Sites detected",
    y = "Carabid genus"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_blank(),                # remove title
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),      # larger axis titles
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(face = "italic", size = 10),  # italic + larger genus labels
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10)
  )


# plot
genus_abund_vy
genus_site_occupancy_vy


# SPECIES ACCUMULATION CURVE
# Aggregate trap-level data to site-level totals
site_species_matrix <- carabid_VY_df %>%
  group_by(site_ID) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(species_columns), ~ sum(as.numeric(.), na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Drop the site_ID column for the matrix
rownames(site_species_matrix) <- site_species_matrix$site_ID
site_species_matrix <- site_species_matrix[ , -1]

# Remove all-zero families
keep <- colSums(site_species_matrix, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
site_species_matrix <- site_species_matrix[, keep, drop = FALSE]

# Build accumulation curve, use random as the method so sites are added randomly
acc_site <- specaccum(site_species_matrix, method = "random", permutations = 1000)

# Prepare tidy dataframe for plotting
acc_site_df <- tibble(
  sites = acc_site$sites,
  richness = acc_site$richness,
  se = acc_site$sd
)

# Plot
carabid_species_accumulation <- ggplot(acc_site_df, aes(x = sites, y = richness)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = richness - 1.96 * se,
                    ymax = richness + 1.96 * se),
                width = 0.3) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of sites",
    y = "Number of carabid species observed") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

carabid_species_accumulation

```

Carabid species richness increased rapidly with the first few sites and continued to rise more gradually, without reaching an asymptotic, indicating that additional sampling may detect more species.

Lets join the predictor variables for the model.

```{r}
# Full combined dataset (with predictor variables)
carabid_df <- carabid_data_VY %>%
  inner_join(predictor_variables, by = c("site_ID", "habitat", "year"))                    

# Remove incomplete rows (sites missing predictor variable data)
# convert others to factors
carabid_df_clean <- carabid_df %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(
    management_type = as.factor(management_type),
    habitat         = factor(habitat, levels = c("CR", "DR")),
    site_ID         = as.factor(site_ID),
    trap_count      = as.numeric(trap_count),
    year = as.factor(year),
  )


```

```{r}
# select carabid abundance and species richness columns

carabid_summary
```

I also want to make summary tables for carabids by 1) management type, 2) habitat and 3) year


```{r}
# carabid abundance and richness summary stats
response_summary_by <- function(data, group_var, group_label) {
  data %>%
    group_by({{ group_var }}) %>%
    summarise(
      carabid_abundance_mean   = mean(carabid_abundance,   na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_abundance_sd     = sd(carabid_abundance,     na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_abundance_min    = min(carabid_abundance,    na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_abundance_max    = max(carabid_abundance,    na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_abundance_median = median(carabid_abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_abundance_IQR    = IQR(carabid_abundance,    na.rm = TRUE),

      carabid_rich_mean        = mean(species_richness,    na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_rich_sd          = sd(species_richness,      na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_rich_min         = min(species_richness,     na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_rich_max         = max(species_richness,     na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_rich_median      = median(species_richness,  na.rm = TRUE),
      carabid_rich_IQR         = IQR(species_richness,     na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Level    = as.character({{ group_var }}), 
      Grouping = group_label
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Grouping, Level, everything(), -{{ group_var }})
}


# 1) By management type
summary_by_mgmt <- response_summary_by(
  carabid_df_clean,
  management_type,
  "Management type"
)

# 2) By habitat
summary_by_habitat <- response_summary_by(
  carabid_df_clean,
  habitat,
  "Habitat"
)

# 3) By year
summary_by_year <- response_summary_by(
  carabid_df_clean,
  year,
  "Year"
)

# Combine into one long table
carabid_response_summary_all <- bind_rows(
  summary_by_mgmt,
  summary_by_habitat,
  summary_by_year
)

carabid_response_summary_all

# save as table
write.csv(
  carabid_response_summary_all,
  here::here("02_tables", "carabid_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

Carabid mean abundance and richness higher in organic vineyards, but also lots of variability. Carabid mean abundance on average higher vine rows compared to inter-rows, and higher in 2025 compared to 2024.

## GLMM's

### Management models
First let's fit models using management type, habitat and year as predictors.

#### Spider abundance

Let's try fitting a GLMM model using poisson distribution first (appropriate for count data).

```{r}
# Fit GLMM model (using Poisson first, then check for overdispersion)
# include site as random effect and offset to account for traps destroyed in field
spider_abund_mgmt_poisson <- glmmTMB(
  spider_abundance ~  management_type + habitat + year + (1 | site_ID) + 
    offset(log(trap_count)),
  data = spider_df_clean,
  family = "poisson"
)

# Check the summary of the model
summary(spider_abund_mgmt_poisson)

```


Let's check to see if the model meets the assumptions by evaluating the residuals using DHARMa package

```{r}
# NORMALITY OF RESIDUALS
# Model diagnostics
residuals_poisson <- simulateResiduals(spider_abund_mgmt_poisson)
plot(residuals_poisson)

```

Problems with the residuals, lets switch to negative binomial. 

```{r}
# problems detected, switch to negative binomial
# use scaled continuous variables to make comparisons based on effect size
spider_abund_mgmt_nb <- glmmTMB(
  spider_abundance ~ management_type + habitat + year + (1 | site_ID) +
    offset(log(trap_count)),
  data = spider_df_clean,
  family = "nbinom1"
)

# Check the summary of the model
summary(spider_abund_mgmt_nb)

# Check performance (marginal and condition R-squared)
performance::r2(spider_abund_mgmt_nb)

```



##### Meeting model assumptions
```{r}
# Model diagnostics
spider_residuals_nb <- simulateResiduals(spider_abund_mgmt_nb)
plot(spider_residuals_nb)
```


Residuals look good! Conditional R2 0.74, marginal 0.33. Not bad, random and fixed effects explaining quite a bit of the variability in the data.

Let's check for colinearity of the predictor variables and spatial autocorrelation in residuals to verify independence of sampling points.

```{r}
# INDEPENDENCE

# Check for outliers/ influential values
DHARMa::testOutliers(spider_abund_mgmt_nb)


# Check for spatial autocorrelation
# prepare coordinates
coords <- coords %>%
  mutate(
    site_ID = as.character(site_ID),
    long = as.numeric(gsub("c\\(|\\)", "", as.character(long))),
    lat  = as.numeric(as.character(lat))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(long)) %>%
  distinct(site_ID, .keep_all = TRUE)          # one row per site

# test using dharma
# Make sure site_ID types match and join to model data
data_dharma_spider <- spider_df_clean %>%
  mutate(site_ID = as.character(site_ID)) %>%
  left_join(coords, by = "site_ID")

# Simulate DHARMa residuals
sim_res_spider <- simulateResiduals(spider_abund_mgmt_nb, plot = FALSE)

# recalculate per site
sim_res_site_spider <- recalculateResiduals(sim_res_spider, group = data_dharma_spider$site_ID)

# aggregate coordinates by site
coords_site_spider <- data_dharma_spider %>%
  group_by(site_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    long = first(long),
    lat  = first(lat),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(site_ID)

# Spatial autocorrelation test (coords repeated for each observation at same site)
testSpatialAutocorrelation(
  sim_res_site_spider,
  x = coords_site_spider$long,
  y = coords_site_spider$lat
)

```
No significant residual outliers

No spatial autocorrelation detected based on DHARMa Moran's I.

Model meets independence assumptions.

##### Model outputs

Make a figure displaying the model results with confidence intervals.

```{r}
# Tidy fixed effects with 95% CIs (log scale)
fx_spider_abund_mgmt <- tidy(spider_abund_mgmt_nb, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    term_label = dplyr::recode(term,
                               "management_typeorg"   = "Management: Organic",
                               "habitatDR"            = "Inter-row Habitat",
                               "year"             = "Year: 2025"
    ),
    sig = p.value < 0.05
  )


# plot GLMM model fixed effects
p_log_spider_abund_mgmt <- ggplot(fx_spider_abund_mgmt, aes(x = estimate, y = term_label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high,
                     alpha = ifelse(sig, 1, 0.5)), height = 0.18) +
  geom_point(aes(alpha = ifelse(sig, 1, 0.5)), size = 2.8) +
  scale_alpha_identity() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Spider Abundance") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_log_spider_abund_mgmt

```


Organic management and year significant, but lots of variability (wide confidence intervals)


#### Spider richness

```{r}
# Fit GLMM with interaction
spider_richness_mgmt_poisson <- glmmTMB(
  family_richness ~ management_type + habitat + year + (1 | site_ID) +
    offset(log(trap_count)),
  data = spider_df_clean,
  family = "poisson",
  na.action = na.fail
)


summary(spider_richness_mgmt_poisson)

```

##### Meeting model assumptions

```{r}
# Diagnostics with DHARMa
sim_res_rich <- simulateResiduals(spider_richness_mgmt_poisson)
plot(sim_res_rich)              # QQ + residual vs predicted
testDispersion(sim_res_rich)

```

Dipsersion problems detected, lets switch to conway-maxwell to deal with underdispersion.

```{r}
# significant problems detected, lets try conway-maxwell to deal with underdispersion
# add an optimizer to tell it to still run (even if it takes a long time!)
spider_richness_mgmt_compois <- glmmTMB(
  family_richness ~ management_type + habitat + year + (1 | site_ID) +
    offset(log(trap_count)),
  data = spider_df_clean,
  family = compois(),
  control = glmmTMBControl(
    optimizer = optim,
    optArgs = list(method = "BFGS"),
    profile = TRUE
  )
)


summary(spider_richness_mgmt_compois)

```


```{r}
# Check residuals
spider_residuals_compois <- simulateResiduals(spider_richness_mgmt_compois)
plot(spider_residuals_compois)


# Check performance (marginal and condition R-squared)
performance::r2(spider_richness_mgmt_compois)

# Check for outliers/ influential values
DHARMa::testOutliers(spider_residuals_compois)

```


Residuals look okay! 

Marginal R2 suggests that richness is fairly random across sites, and predictors don’t add much explanatory power.


##### Model outputs
Let's make another plot looking at the model outputs

```{r}
# recalculate per site
sim_res_site_carabid_rich <- recalculateResiduals(sim_res_carabid_rich, group = data_dharma_carabids$site_ID)

# aggregate coordinates by site
coords_site_carabids <- data_dharma_carabids %>%
  group_by(site_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    long = first(long),
    lat  = first(lat),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(site_ID)

# Spatial autocorrelation test (coords repeated for each observation at same site)
testSpatialAutocorrelation(
  sim_res_site_carabid_rich,
  x = coords_site_carabids$long,
  y = coords_site_carabids$lat
)

```

No evidence of spatial autocorrelation or influential residual outliers

##### Sensitivity analysis: landscape scale

We'll check and see if any of the different scales (100-1000m) impact the response variables


Next we'll fit models for each of the different scales
```{r}
# Define the scales
scales <- c(100, 250, 500, 750, 1000)

# identify columns
nat_cols <- paste0("z_total_natural_", scales)
nat_cols
# [1] "z_total_natural_100" ... etc

# Build a function to fit the model for a given natural-cover scale
spider_abund_scale <- function(nat_col, data = spider_df_clean) {

  # Create the formula programmatically so only nat_col changes
  f <- as.formula(paste(
    "spider_abundance ~",
    "z_veg_height + z_veg_cover + z_veg_richness +",
    nat_col, "+ z_distance_natural + year +",
    "(1 | site_ID) + offset(log(trap_count))"
  ))

  glmmTMB(
    formula = f,
    data = data,
    family = nbinom2()
  )
}

# Fit all scales 
spider_abund_fit <- setNames(
  lapply(nat_cols, spider_abund_scale),
  paste0(scales, "m")
)

# Compare model fit across scales (AIC) 
spider_abund_aic <- tibble(
  scale = names(spider_abund_fit),
  AIC = sapply(spider_abund_fit, AIC)
) %>%
  arrange(AIC) %>%
  mutate(delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC))

spider_abund_aic

# Extract the effect of "total natural" at each scale (estimate + CI)
# This pulls the coefficient that matches the nat_col used in each model.
spider_abund_coef <- imap_dfr(spider_abund_fit, function(mod, scale_nm){

  nat_term <- paste0("z_total_natural_", sub("m", "", scale_nm))

  broom.mixed::tidy(mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == nat_term) %>%
    mutate(scale = scale_nm) %>%
    select(scale, term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, std.error, statistic, p.value)
})

spider_abund_coef %>% arrange(as.numeric(sub("m","", scale)))

# quick DHARMa residual diagnostics across scales
dharma_res <- imap(spider_abund_fit, ~simulateResiduals(.x, n = 1000))

# Plot each
walk2(dharma_res, names(dharma_res), ~{
  plot(.x, main = paste("DHARMa residuals:", .y), cex.main = 0.9)
})

```

Proportion of natural habitat not an important predictor at any scale. 
No difference between scales based on AIC (delta AIC <2)

#### Spider family richness

```{r}
# Fit GLMM with interaction
spider_richness_poisson <- glmmTMB(
  family_richness ~ management_type + habitat + z_veg_height + z_veg_cover + z_veg_richness + z_total_natural_500 + year + (1 | site_ID) +
    offset(log(trap_count)),
  data = spider_df_clean,
  family = "poisson",
  na.action = na.fail
)


summary(spider_richness_poisson)

```

Problems detected, lets switch to conway-maxwell to deal with underdispersion.

```{r}
# Fit GLMM with conway maxwell, optimize so it doesn't quit
spider_richness_compois <- glmmTMB(
  family_richness ~ z_veg_height + z_veg_cover + z_veg_richness + z_total_natural_500 + z_distance_natural + year + (1 | site_ID) + 
    offset(log(trap_count)),
  data = spider_df_clean,
  family = compois(),
  control = glmmTMBControl(
    optimizer = optim,
    optArgs = list(method = "BFGS"),
    profile = TRUE
  )
)


summary(spider_richness_compois)


```
##### Meeting model assumptions

```{r}
# Check residuals
spider_residuals_compois <- simulateResiduals(spider_richness_compois)
plot(spider_residuals_compois)


# Check performance (marginal and condition R-squared)
performance::r2(spider_richness_compois)
```

##### Sensitivity analysis: landscape scale

```{r}

# Build a function to fit the model for a given natural-cover scale
carabid_abund_scale <- function(nat_col, data = carabid_df_clean) {

  # Create the formula programmatically so only nat_col changes
  f <- as.formula(paste(
    "carabid_abundance ~",
    "z_veg_height + z_veg_cover + z_veg_richness +",
    nat_col, "+ z_distance_natural + year +",
    "(1 | site_ID) + offset(log(trap_count))"
  ))

  glmmTMB(
    formula = f,
    data = data,
    family = nbinom1()
  )
}

# Fit all scales 
carabid_abund_fit <- setNames(
  lapply(nat_cols, carabid_abund_scale),
  paste0(scales, "m")
)

# Compare model fit across scales (AIC) 
carabid_abund_aic <- tibble(
  scale = names(carabid_abund_fit),
  AIC = sapply(carabid_abund_fit, AIC)
) %>%
  arrange(AIC) %>%
  mutate(delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC))

carabid_abund_aic

# Extract the effect of "total natural" at each scale (estimate + CI)
# This pulls the coefficient that matches the nat_col used in each model.
carabid_abund_coef <- imap_dfr(carabid_abund_fit, function(mod, scale_nm){

  nat_term <- paste0("z_total_natural_", sub("m", "", scale_nm))

  broom.mixed::tidy(mod, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == nat_term) %>%
    mutate(scale = scale_nm) %>%
    select(scale, term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, std.error, statistic, p.value)
})

carabid_abund_coef %>% arrange(as.numeric(sub("m","", scale)))
```

Proportion of natural habitat not an important predictor at any scale. 
No difference between scales based on AIC (delta AIC <2)

```{r}
# Fit GLMM model (using Poisson first, then check for overdispersion)
#Site as random effect
carabid_richness_poisson <- glmmTMB(
  species_richness ~ z_veg_height + z_veg_cover + z_veg_richness + z_total_natural_500 + z_distance_natural + year + (1 | site_ID) + 
    offset(log(trap_count)),
  data = carabid_df_clean,
  family = "poisson",
  na.action = na.fail
)

summary(carabid_richness_poisson)


```



##### Meeting model assumptions

```{r}
# Check residuals
carabid_residuals_poisson <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(carabid_richness_poisson)
plot(carabid_residuals_poisson)



# Check performance (marginal and condition R-squared)
performance::r2(carabid_richness_poisson)
```
Residuals look okay!

No evidence of influential outliers in residuals. 

Conditional R2 ~0.21, which means some of the variability is explained by between site differences. 
Marginal R2 very low (0.04) which means predictor variables have very little explanatory power. 



```{r}
# Testing for spatial autocorrelation
# test using dharma
# Simulate DHARMa residuals
sim_res_carabid_rich <- simulateResiduals(carabid_richness_poisson, plot = FALSE)

# recalculate per site
sim_res_site_carabid_rich <- recalculateResiduals(sim_res_carabid_rich, group = data_dharma_carabids$site_ID)

# aggregate coordinates by site
coords_site_carabids <- data_dharma_carabids %>%
  group_by(site_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    long = first(long),
    lat  = first(lat),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(site_ID)

# Spatial autocorrelation test (coords repeated for each observation at same site)
testSpatialAutocorrelation(
  sim_res_site_carabid_rich,
  x = coords_site_carabids$long,
  y = coords_site_carabids$lat
)

```

### Model Summaries and Outputs

Output table for GLMM model results


#### Management 

```{r}
# helper function
tidy_glmm <- function(model, response_label) {
  tidy(model, effects = "fixed") %>%
    # drop intercept or keep it; here we keep it and give a label
    dplyr::mutate(
      Predictor = dplyr::recode(
        term,
        "management_typeorg"  = "Management: Organic",
        "habitatDR"           = "Inter-row habitat",
        "year2025"            = "Year (2025)",   # if present
        .default = term       # 
      ),
      Response = response_label
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Response, Predictor, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value)
}

# create table for each response variable
tab_spider_abund_mgmt   <- tidy_glmm(spider_abund_mgmt_nb,   "Spider abundance")
tab_spider_rich_mgmt    <- tidy_glmm(spider_richness_mgmt_compois,    "Spider family richness")
tab_carabid_abund_mgmt  <- tidy_glmm(carabid_abund_mgmt_nb,  "Carabid abundance")
tab_carabid_rich_mgmt   <- tidy_glmm(carabid_richness_mgmt_poisson,   "Carabid species richness")

# combine tables
model_results_mgmt <- bind_rows(
  tab_spider_rich_mgmt,
  tab_spider_abund_mgmt,
  tab_carabid_rich_mgmt,
  tab_carabid_abund_mgmt
)

# clean up numbers
model_results_mgmt_clean <- model_results_mgmt %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Estimate = round(estimate, 2),
    SE       = round(std.error, 2),
    z        = round(statistic, 2),
    p_raw    = p.value,
    p        = case_when(
      p_raw < 0.001 ~ "< 0.001",
      TRUE          ~ sprintf("%.3f", p_raw)
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Response, Predictor, Estimate, SE, z, p) %>%
  arrange(Response, Predictor) 

# save as table
write.csv(
  model_results_mgmt_clean,
  here::here("02_tables", "model_results_mgmt_clean.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# get group indices
kable(
  model_results_mgmt_clean,
  col.names = c("Response variable", "Predictors", "Estimate", "SE", "z", "p"),
  align    = "llrrrr",
  booktabs = TRUE,
  caption  = "GLMM results for spider and carabid responses.",
  escape   = FALSE        # important for bold p-values
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
```






And a final figure for GLMM model results

```{r}
# labels for predictor variables
predictor_levels <- c(
  "Year: 2025",
  "Management: Organic",
  "Inter-row Habitat"
)

# specify plot parameters
make_effect_plot <- function(fx, panel_title, xlim = c(-0.5, 1.2), show_y_labels = TRUE) {

  fx <- fx %>%
    mutate(
      term_label = factor(term_label, levels = rev(predictor_levels)),
      col = ifelse(sig, "sig", "nonsig")
    )

  p <- ggplot(fx, aes(x = estimate, y = term_label)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.5, colour = "grey40") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                   height = 0.18, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
    geom_point(aes(fill = col), shape = 21, size = 2.8, stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(sig = "black", nonsig = "grey70"), guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = panel_title) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90"),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8)
    )

  if (!show_y_labels) {
    p <- p + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                   axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
  }

  return(p)
}

# make plot for each response variable
# only show the y axis labels for figures on the left
pA <- make_effect_plot(fx_spider_abund_mgmt,     "Spider abundance",       show_y_labels = TRUE)
pB <- make_effect_plot(fx_spider_richness_mgmt,      "Spider richness",        show_y_labels = FALSE)
pC <- make_effect_plot(fx_carabid_abund_mgmt,    "Carabid abundance",      show_y_labels = TRUE)
pD <- make_effect_plot(fx_carabid_richness_mgmt, "Carabid richness",       show_y_labels = FALSE)


# combine model output figures
p_log_all <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  pA, pB,
  pC, pD,
  labels = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  label_size = 10,
  ncol = 2
)

# add x axis label at the bottom
final_model_output <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  p_log_all,
  ggdraw() + draw_label("Estimate (log scale)", size = 10),
  ncol = 1,
  rel_heights = c(1, 0.05)
)

final_model_output


# save to figures folder
ggsave(
  filename = here::here("03_figures", "final_mgmt_output.png"),
  plot = final_model_output,
  width = 7,      
  height = 5,     
  dpi = 300       # high-resolution
)

```

```{r}
  rel_heights = c(1.5, 0.05)
)

final_model_output_year





```

Make a table showing the model outputs for response variables modelled independently by year

```{r}
# create table for each response variable
tab_spider_abund_2024   <- tidy_glmm(spider_abund_2024,   "Spider abundance 2024")
tab_spider_abund_2025   <- tidy_glmm(spider_abund_2025,    "Spider abundance 2025")
tab_carabid_abund_2024  <- tidy_glmm(carabid_abund_2024,  "Carabid abundance 2024")
tab_carabid_abund_2025   <- tidy_glmm(carabid_abund_2025,   "Carabid abundance 2025")

# combine tables
model_results_years <- bind_rows(
  tab_spider_abund_2024,
  tab_spider_abund_2025,
  tab_carabid_abund_2024,
  tab_carabid_abund_2025
)

# clean up numbers
model_results_years_clean <- model_results_years %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Estimate = round(estimate, 2),
    SE       = round(std.error, 2),
    z        = round(statistic, 2),
    p_raw    = p.value,
    p        = case_when(
      p_raw < 0.001 ~ "< 0.001",
      TRUE          ~ sprintf("%.3f", p_raw)
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Response, Predictor, Estimate, SE, z, p) %>%
  arrange(Response, Predictor) 

# save as table
write.csv(
  model_results_years_clean,
  here::here("02_tables", "model_results_years_clean.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)


# get group indices
kable(
  model_results_years_clean,
  col.names = c("Response variable", "Predictors", "Estimate", "SE", "z", "p"),
  align    = "llrrrr",
  booktabs = TRUE,
  caption  = "GLMM results for spider and carabid responses.",
  escape   = FALSE        # important for bold p-values
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
```
